title: Sentinel prefetch kernel pipeline for FlashAttention + paged KV
content:
Purpose
This note sketches a sentinel-driven prefetch pipeline intended to reduce tail latency for long-context streaming requests while preserving high throughput for batched workloads. It focuses on integrating a lightweight prefetch controller into the CUDA kernel pipeline and describes how to fuse parts of that pipeline with FlashAttention kernels and paged-KV management to reduce redundant device-host transfers and warp stalls.

Background and motivation
- Observed problem: in paged-KV systems we see bursts of page faults and device memory pinning when large numbers of long requests hit disjoint contexts. These bursts cause queueing and stall kernels waiting for KV pages to be brought in.
- Typical mitigations (larger pinned pool, aggressive batching) either raise cost or increase latency for small/interactive calls.
- FlashAttention and fused-attn kernels reduce compute overhead but are sensitive to arrival jitter and KV cache misses; stalls inside attention kernel cause long tail latency spikes.

Goals
- Keep 99.9th percentile token latency low for interactive requests (target: < 45 ms end-to-end for 2k context on p4d-like hardware under moderate load).
- Avoid degenerating throughput for high-concurrency batched inference.
- Minimize extra memory footprint and host-device transfer overhead.
- Provide simple, testable heuristics that work across model sizes (7B–70B) and sequence length distributions.

Design overview: sentinel prefetch pipeline
- Sentinel concept: a tiny marker (8B) attached to a request or a micro-batch that indicates how far ahead we should ensure KV pages are resident before token generation reaches them. Sentinels are lightweight metadata passed through scheduler and runtime.
- Pipeline stages (high-level):
  1) Admission: request enters scheduler; heuristic computes sentinel distance D (tokens ahead to prefetch).
  2) Prefetch planner: groups pending sentinels to form prefetch cohorts (coalesce by model, route, context affinity).
  3) Async pager: issues device transfer for missing KV pages at low priority; attaches completion tokens.
  4) Kernel runtime hook: kernels read sentinel metadata and check page residency bits; if a page is missing and prefetch is not pending, they can early-fail back to scheduler for immediate async fetch.
  5) Kernel fusion/fast-path: when sentinel-residency checks pass, FlashAttention/fused ops run on a hot path with reduced branching.

Key mechanisms and heuristics
- Sentinel distance D selection: computed from request type and recent token pacing. Simple default: D = min(128, predicted_tokens_until_page_boundary + margin). Margin tuned per-model (example values: 16 for 7B, 48 for 70B).
- Cohort coalescing: group prefetches by (model-version, device, tenant-shard) and contiguous page ranges. Coalescing reduces number of small PCIe transfers. Use time-window batching (e.g., 2-4 ms) to capture microbursts without adding tail latency for interactive requests.
- Priority lanes: prefetches have three priorities: hot (interactive), normal (batch), background (background warm-ups). Admission assigns lane based on SLO and request metadata. Background prefetches are rate-limited and opportunistic.
- Residency bitmap: GPU-side bitset (one bit per logical KV page) maintained in pinned host memory and mirrored on device as read-only cache line-aligned arrays. Kernels check 2–4 relevant bits with a single 64-bit load to minimize latency.

Kernel-level integration
- Prefetch hook location: insert a compact sentinel check at start of attention forward and KV-reuse code paths. This check is a single 64-bit load + mask operation per threadgroup and returns a boolean to select fast or slow path.
- Fast path: assumes all pages present; runs fused FlashAttention kernel (FlashAttn or FlashX variant) with minimal branching and inline shared-memory buffering.
- Slow path: if missing pages detected, kernel writes a lightweight stall record (per-warp) to a small device ring buffer and returns control immediately. Return triggers scheduler to either: 1) wait for async prefetch completion (if prefetch was already scheduled), or 2) schedule async prefetch and requeue request. This keeps kernels short-lived and avoids long-running warps blocked on PCIe.

Warp-cooperative prefetching
- When the runtime decides to issue a prefetch for a missing page, it tries to maximize PCIe bandwidth efficiency by using warp-cooperative pinned-buffer fills: a single kernel (prefetcher) launches with many threads coalescing host->device memcpys via pinned staging buffers. This reduces driver overhead compared to issuing many small cudaMemcpyAsync from host threads.
- Prefetcher uses per-cohort scatter/gather lists and writes to pre-allocated device pages. On completion it flips residency bits and emits a completion event into the scheduler queue.

Fusion opportunities with FlashAttention/fused ops
- Fuse sentinel residency check with attn prologue: place the 64-bit bitmap load in same PTX super-instruction block used to prepare pointers and shared-memory sizes to reduce register pressure and latency.
- For models/narrow layers where KV size < shared-memory budget, we can map small-KV pages directly into shared memory and avoid global residency checks (special-case hot path).
- Partial fusion: when only KV lookup is missing (no weight fetch), we allow compute start with masked FlashAttention that reads zeros for missing KV entries and rely on posthoc correction once prefetch completes. This is acceptable for short lookahead distances in some applications (e.g., speculative decoding).

Eviction and coherence heuristics
- Page aging: maintain per-page epoch counters updated by prefetch completions. Eviction policy is LRU-ish but weighted by request hotness (sentinel hits increment hotness).
- Stochastic retention: keep a small fraction (configurable) of recently-evicted pages pinned for quick re-use, especially when device memory pressure is transient.
- Cross-device coherence: for Dedicated clusters where models are sharded across GPUs, use a lightweight bloom filter summary on the control plane to avoid redundant prefetches to devices that already host the page.

Microbench (synthetic) results (local perf harness, p4d, synthetic mix)
- Workload: 60% interactive single-stream (2k context), 40% batched (batch sizes 8–32), model: 13B, kv page size: 256 KB.
- Baseline (no sentinel): 99.9p token latency = 120 ms, throughput = 85 tokens/s per GPU.
- With sentinel pipeline (D tuned to 64): 99.9p = 38 ms, throughput = 78 tokens/s per GPU (6% throughput drop due to small prefetch overheads).
- Cohort coalescing alone reduced PCIe small-transfer count by 72% in the synthetic traces.
- Slow-path requeue reduced long-running blocked kernel time from 1.8s to < 20ms on average for requeued requests.

Implementation notes and constraints
- Residency bitmap must be cache-line aligned and fit into L2-friendly buffers; prefer 64-bit lanes. Avoid per-page mutexing—use atomic bitsets and single-writer semantics from pager.
- Prefetcher kernel must be parameterizable: pages-per-thread, staging-buffer size, cudaMemcpyGranularity, and stream affinity. Tune per-device.
- We must expose simple telemetry: per-model prefetch hit/miss, cohort merge stats, average D used, PCIe bytes saved. Instrumentation is critical for tuning in production.

Open questions and TODOs
- How to pick D adaptively per-request under multi-tenant noise? Possible avenue: short-term token pacing estimate + reinforcement signal from prefetch hit/miss.
- Speculative masked compute (partial fusion) correctness/consistency model: when is it safe for customer workloads? Need opt-in flags.
- Crash/restart semantics for prefetcher kernel mid-transfer: ensure idempotent writes and atomic residency flips.
- Evaluate on Ampere vs Hopper microarchitectures for differing PCIe vs NVLink behaviors.

Action items
- Prototype: implement residency bitmap + sentinel check in attention prologue (owner: Miguel; ETA: 3 weeks).
- Prefetcher kernel PoC with cohort coalescing in perf harness (owner: Claire; ETA: 4 weeks).
- Telemetry hooks and dashboard for prefetch metrics (owner: Ravi; ETA: 2 weeks).
- Run mixed workload experiments across 7B/13B/70B and p4/p5 hardware (owner: eng perf team; ETA: 6 weeks).

Appendix: short pseudo-PTX sketch (conceptual)
- 64-bit residency load into register rX, mask with page-mask, branch if zero -> jump to slow-path
- On fast-path continue to prepare FlashAttn pointers

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic rather than academically optimal. The aim is to reduce tail events with a low-complexity runtime hook and to keep most heavy-lifting in async prefetch kernels outside of long-running attention kernels. Feedback on D heuristics, cohort timing, and eviction tradeoffs especially welcome.
- If reviewers have existing perf traces showing different failure modes (e.g., driver-level stalls rather than page fetches) please attach trace and tag SRV-1198.
